statement: Let \(a, b, c, d\) be integers with \(ad \neq bc\). Show that \(\dfrac{1}{(ax+b)(cx+d)}\) can be written in the form \(\dfrac{r}{ax+b} + \dfrac{s}{cx+d}\). Hence find the sum \(\dfrac{1}{1 \cdot 4} + \dfrac{1}{4 \cdot 7} + \dfrac{1}{7 \cdot 10} + \cdots + \dfrac{1}{2998 \cdot 3001}\).
Given \(n\) points in the plane, show that we can always find three of them that determine an angle \(\leq \pi/n\).
A convex quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle of radius \(1\). Show that its perimeter minus the sum of its two diagonals lies between \(0\) and \(2\).
Let \(a, b, c, d\) be integers. Show that \(x^2 + ax + b = y^2 + cy + d\) has infinitely many integer solutions if and only if \(a^2 - 4b = c^2 - 4d\).
Let \(A\), \(B\) be real numbers. Find a necessary and sufficient condition for \(Ax + B\lfloor x \rfloor = Ay + B\lfloor y \rfloor\) to have no solutions other than \(x = y\).
